quotes.text: All patient records originate from a de-identified hospital database collected during routine care between 2008 and 2019.

rationale: The paper states the original source type and time frame. It does not give a dataset version or a route from an individual benchmark task to its source record, so this is partial.

quotes.text: approved under a data use agreement requiring credentialed access and de-identification by the safe harbour method

rationale: The paper documents real patient-record origin, routine-care collection, data-use terms, de-identification, and approval status. It also distinguishes data terms from the MIT code licence.

searched: S1-S5. The only representativeness comparison appears in S4 code comments, which do not count as reporting under G1a. The public paper/docs excerpts do not report representativeness against a target population.

quotes.text: We report accuracy per task family (diagnosis, ordering and documentation tasks) and per patient subgroup by sex and race

rationale: The packet reports patient-subgroup results by sex and race, which counts as a bias test. Unsafe or dangerous outputs are measured in scoring, but no dedicated unsafe-output test is reported.

quotes.text: A private held-out test split with concealed labels is excluded from all public surfaces. Released tasks include a canary string.

rationale: The paper reports developer-side contamination controls: a private held-out split and a canary. It does not report a measured overlap or contamination check, so this is partial.

quotes.text: the answer labels are stored in a separate evaluation service that has no network path from the agent sandbox

rationale: The paper states the agent cannot reach ground-truth answers at runtime. It names mechanisms: separate evaluation service, no network path, and labels not published in the repository.

quotes.text: the database snapshot, the software image and the simulated-patient language model are all pinned to fixed versions

rationale: The paper reports pinned data, software image, and simulated-patient model. It also says no external service is called at evaluation time other than the model under test.

quotes.text: we ran a scripted reference solution for each task through the grader; all 120 reference solutions were graded correct

rationale: The appendix reports a scripted reference solution for each task. It states all 120 were run through the grader and graded correct.

quotes.text: Grading validates both intended state modifications and preservation of unrelated records.

rationale: The paper reports that grading checks intended state changes and unchanged unrelated records. That satisfies detection of out-of-scope side effects.

quotes.text: Across all 120 tasks, an agent with no actions scores 0.0%, while a random-action agent achieves 2.5%.

rationale: The paper reports empirical trivial and random-agent rates. Those rates show random or trivial success is unlikely.

quotes.text: Across all 120 tasks, an agent with no actions scores 0.0%, while a random-action agent achieves 2.5%.

rationale: The benchmark reports a no-actions agent score and a random-action score across all 120 tasks. This satisfies the all-task trivial-agent result anchor.

quotes.text: Diagnosis agreement | Diag. kappa | Evidence corr. | Plan corr.

rationale: The appendix reports validation of manager-side scoring on 100 sampled final outputs with physician audit figures. It gives agreement, kappa, and correlation metrics for benchmark outputs.

quotes.text: Every run applies temperature 0 with a fixed seed. The main text describes the policy of executing each task three times.

rationale: The paper reports both temperature 0 with a fixed seed and a repeated-run policy. That satisfies the full anchor.

quotes.text: test the difference between the two best models with a paired permutation test (p = 0.02)

rationale: The appendix reports confidence intervals and a paired permutation test for a model comparison. This meets the headline comparison uncertainty/significance anchor.

quotes.text: Every run applies temperature 0 with a fixed seed. The main text describes the policy of executing each task three times.

rationale: The packet states the number of runs per task and the seed/decoding policy. It does not state whether the runs are independent, so only two of three elements are present.

quotes.text: where several tasks share a patient, we resample patients instead to account for clustering

rationale: The paper reports 95% bootstrap confidence intervals, names the task as the resampling unit, and addresses clustering by patient. All three elements are present.

quotes.text: report pass^8, the fraction of tasks solved in all eight runs

rationale: The appendix reports pass^8 with eight runs and agreement of final environment state across reruns. It does not report action-sequence agreement, but either all-runs or state-level agreement with run count is enough for full credit.

quotes.text: snapshot identifiers gpt-4o-2024-08-06 and claude-3-5-sonnet-20241022

rationale: The appendix gives exact model snapshot identifiers, temperature and token parameters, and states that reported numbers correspond to harness release v1.2.0. All three pinning elements are present.

quotes.text: Schemas, manifests, and Croissant metadata | Validate case, episode, event-log, score, memory, and process files

rationale: The benchmark defines an action/tool-like interface and reports schemas plus return-result status and invalid-test categories. It does not document side effects per tool on S1-S3 or S5 in the packet, so only partial elements are present.

searched: S1-S5. The packet does not report tests or conformance checks showing tools behave as documented. It also does not report any simulated, stubbed, or no-op tool disclosure reaching the agent-visible surface.

searched: S1-S5. S4 mentions write actions that change patient state, so the item is applicable, but S4 code comments do not count as reporting. No qualifying S1-S3 or S5 disclosure of write actions, sandboxing, or penalties is present.

quotes.text: The grader takes the final environment state as its input.

rationale: The paper states the grader input is the final environment state. It also reports validation on injected correct and incorrect outcomes with false-accept and false-reject rates, so full credit applies despite no non-state-grader rationale being needed.

quotes.text: Web access is blocked during runs; retrieval is confined to the task environment

rationale: The paper reports controls on web and retrieval leakage, a private held-out split with concealed labels, and a canary string. All three agent-channel contamination elements are present.

quotes.text: each table lists the number of cases in every slice

rationale: The paper reports accuracy per task family and per patient subgroup by sex and race. It also states that each slice table lists the number of cases.

quotes.text: The patient records are real de-identified records from a hospital database.

rationale: The packet states the environment records are real de-identified hospital data. It also reports DUA, credentialed access, safe-harbour de-identification, approval, and data terms separate from the MIT code licence.
